title: DeepSeek Prover vs. US Models on Security Tasks: Empirical Test of the US-China Formal Verification Gap

original_idea.body:
# DeepSeek Prover vs. US Models on Security Tasks: Empirical Test of the US-China Formal Verification Gap

**Problem:** RAND (2026) claims Chinese models (DeepSeek, ByteDance) lead in AI theorem proving while US frontier labs have not prioritized this. An empirical test on security-specific formal verification tasks would validate or challenge this claim.

**Direction:** Run DeepSeek-Prover V2 (or latest available) and US frontier models (Claude, GPT-4) on VeriBench's security challenge subset and a curated security-specific formal verification set. Measure compilation rate, proof success, and failure mode distribution. Report as a head-to-head comparison.

**Why it matters:** RAND's policy recommendation depends on this capability gap being real. If US models are competitive, the policy urgency is different. If Chinese models do lead specifically on security-relevant formal verification, this is critical for national security planning.

**Relevant context:** RAND (Sarma & Fisher, February 2026) explicitly names DeepSeek and ByteDance. DeepSeek-Prover has achieved state-of-the-art on formal theorem proving benchmarks. No published comparison exists on security-specific tasks.
